Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: Act 025/2023 (Personal Data Protection Law) explicitly grants individuals the right to obtain all their personal data in an understandable form, to rectify it, and to request deletion. The APDPVP must respond to access requests from data subjects (Article 52/53). This right extends to data held in the national ID system.
revision_notes: Original Value Code (1=No) was inconsistent with the cited Comments, which already described statutory rights of data access extending to the ID system. Verified: Act 025/2023 Arts 43-44 provide a free, written formal-request mechanism for individuals to obtain a copy of their personal data; APDPVP Deliberation No. 026/2023 (14 Nov 2023) on the IBOGA biometric ID system designates the DGDI as the service for exercising the right of access and rectification. No self-service portal identified - access is via formal request. Score corrected to 2=Yes.
revised_comments: Act No. 025/2023 (amending Act No. 001/2011) grants a general right of access: individuals may submit a free written request to obtain confirmation of, and a copy of, personal data held about them (Articles 43-44). The APDPVP's Deliberation No. 026/2023 of 14 November 2023, authorising data processing under the IBOGA biometric identification system used for the electronic national ID card (CNIE), explicitly designates the Direction Générale de la Documentation et de l'Immigration as the service through which the right of access and rectification is exercised. Access is via formal request rather than a self-service online portal.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: The 2023 data protection law (Act 025/2023) gives the APDPVP authority to submit observations to the Public Prosecutor, initiate investigations, and impose sanctions. Courts have oversight over APDPVP decisions (data controllers can appeal to the State Counsel). However, the World Bank project notes that the CNPDCP/APDPVP has limited capacity to fully carry out its mandate.
revision_notes: Fetched cited sources (DLA Piper, World Bank Digital Gabon PAD P175987). Confirmed APDPVP decisions are subject to appeal through ordinary courts under Act 025/2023 but no ID-specific judicial mechanism exists. World Bank document confirms CNPDCP/APDPVP institutional capacity constraints and references CNPDCP by name. Score of 2 (Yes, but not specific to ID) is well supported; confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Act 025/2023 establishes the APDPVP with powers to investigate complaints, impose sanctions and refer matters to the Public Prosecutor. Decisions of the APDPVP affecting data controllers can be appealed through the ordinary courts, but no ID-specific judicial review mechanism exists. The World Bank's Digital Gabon project (P175987) notes that the CNPDCP/APDPVP has limited institutional capacity to fully exercise its mandate.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Act 025/2023 establishes rules for data interconnection requiring non-discrimination, appropriate security measures, and proportionality. Cross-border transfers are restricted to countries with adequate protection. The World Bank Digital Gabon project requires that databases of the RBPP, civil registration, and national ID card systems NOT be integrated (kept separate) per legal covenant. Formal interoperability framework with data sharing rules is still under development.
revision_notes: Fetched cited sources. World Bank Digital Gabon PAD (P175987) confirms a legal covenant keeping RBPP, civil registration and national ID databases functionally separate, and references a Common Interoperability Framework (CIF) still under development, consistent with 'Partially available'. Confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Act 025/2023 establishes general procedural rules for the collection, processing, storage and sharing of personal data, including requirements of non-discrimination, security and proportionality for data interconnection, and restrictions on cross-border transfers to countries without adequate protection. Under the World Bank-financed Digital Gabon project, a legal covenant requires that the databases of the Biometric Registry of Physical Persons (RBPP), civil registration and the national ID card remain functionally separate rather than merged, and a Common Interoperability Framework governing data-sharing rules across these systems remains under development.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Gabon has a comprehensive Data Protection Act: Law No. 025/2023 of 09/07/2023 amending Law No. 001/2011 of 25 September 2011 on the protection of personal data. This establishes the APDPVP (Authority for the Protection of Personal Data and Privacy) as the supervisory authority.
revision_notes: Original Value Code (1=No) directly contradicted the cited Comments and sources, which describe a comprehensive Data Protection Act (Act 025/2023 amending Act 001/2011) establishing the APDPVP. Confirmed via DLA Piper and Clym summaries of the law. Score corrected to 2=Yes.
revised_comments: Gabon's data protection regime is set out in Act No. 025/2023 of 9 July 2023, amending Act No. 001/2011 of 25 September 2011 on the protection of personal data. The law establishes the Autorité pour la Protection des Données Personnelles et de la Vie Privée (APDPVP) as an independent supervisory authority and applies to public and private sector processing of personal data, including biometric data used in identity systems such as IBOGA.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The APDPVP (Autorité pour la Protection des Données Personnelles et de la Vie Privée) was established under Act 025/2023 as an independent supervisory authority. It is empowered to investigate, subpoena evidence, receive complaints, impose sanctions, and conduct inspections on personal data processing including biometric data used in identity systems.
revision_notes: Original Value Code (1=No) contradicted the cited Comments describing the APDPVP's active regulatory powers. Verified via DLA Piper, Clym and, notably, APDPVP Deliberation No. 026/2023 (14 Nov 2023), in which the Authority formally reviewed and approved government plans to access and process personal data in the IBOGA biometric ID system for CNIE issuance - direct evidence of active oversight of the ID system. Score corrected to 2=Yes.
revised_comments: The APDPVP, established under Act 025/2023, is Gabon's independent data protection authority, empowered to investigate, request documents, receive complaints, impose sanctions and issue binding opinions on data processing. It has exercised active oversight of the national ID system: in Deliberation No. 026/APDPVP of 14 November 2023, it issued a formal opinion approving the government's plan to access and extract personal data from the IBOGA biometric identification system for enrolment and issuance of the electronic national ID card (CNIE), including designating the service responsible for handling access and rectification requests.
